headline: New evening confusion with a stove safety event (reported 11/2) has no documented work-up results, and this follows a 9/25 fall and caregiver exhaustion reported 11/22.

items.statement: On 11/2 the grandson Robert reported about two weeks of increased evening confusion, including once leaving the stove on. Jerónimo was oriented to person and place but not date, with no fever. The plan was urinalysis, medication review, and a PCP visit that week. The provided notes do not show results or a visit for this.
items.verifier_note: All details match the 11/2 nursing note. The statement that results and a visit are not shown is consistent with the empty encounters record.

items.statement: Fall at home on 9/25 getting out of bed in the bedroom. His grandson found him on the floor. He denied head strike or loss of consciousness. He had a small left forearm skin tear, which was cleaned and dressed. Fall risk was reassessed as high and a PT referral was placed.
items.verifier_note: Every detail matches the 9/25 nursing note: bedroom, getting out of bed, grandson found him, no head strike or LOC, left forearm skin tear cleaned and dressed, high fall risk, PT referral.

items.statement: On 11/22 Robert, the primary caregiver, reported exhaustion and poor sleep. He is worried about managing evenings alone and requested respite. The social worker discussed respite options and a caregiver support group.
items.verifier_note: Matches the 11/22 social work note: exhaustion, poor sleep, worry about evenings alone, respite request, and discussion of respite options and a support group.

items.statement: PT evaluation on 9/29 found slow, unsteady gait with intermittent cane use and a Timed Up and Go of 19 seconds. PT recommended a front-wheeled walker, a home safety evaluation, and bathroom grab bars, with PT twice weekly for strength and balance. The notes do not show whether the equipment or home evaluation were completed.
items.verifier_note: Matches the 9/29 PT evaluation: gait, cane use, TUG 19 s, walker, home safety evaluation, grab bars, twice weekly. The note does not show completion, as the statement says.

items.statement: No influenza vaccine is recorded for the current season, which started 8/1/2026. The last recorded dose was 6/30/2026, before the season began.
items.verifier_note: No flu vaccine this season (season start 8/1/2026) and the last dose on 6/30/2026 are supported by the record. The record shows a 6/30/2026 influenza dose, which is odd, but the statement matches it. It is only partial because a dose dated before the season start is unusual and the statement does not flag it for verification.

questions_for_team: Were the urinalysis, medication review, and PCP visit planned on 11/2 completed, and what were the results? The 11/13 nursing note says 'no new concerns' and does not mention the confusion.
What interim safety measures are in place for evenings, given the stove incident and a caregiver who is exhausted and alone in the evenings?
How soon can respite be arranged for Robert, and has he been connected to the caregiver support group?
Have the front-wheeled walker, home safety evaluation, and grab bars been put in place since the 9/29 PT recommendations?
Should the influenza vaccine be offered now, given none is recorded this season?

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and pull all encounters, ED visits, and admissions in that window; note any cardiac-related encounters given new ischemic heart disease onset 2026-06-30.
Falls check: any falls or near-falls in the window, injuries, and fall-risk screen, given age 73, osteoporosis, scoliosis, and new antiplatelet/antianginal medications.

Medication reconciliation: verify metoprolol succinate, clopidogrel, nitroglycerin spray, simvastatin, and alendronic acid are being taken as prescribed; check for any starts, stops, or dose changes since last review, and for missed doses.
Bleeding and cardiac symptom review: any bleeding, bruising, GI symptoms, chest pain, nitroglycerin use frequency, dizziness, or syncope since the ischemic heart disease diagnosis.
Blood pressure and heart rate trend in the window, including orthostatic readings, since beta-blocker and nitrate use started in July 2026.
Lipid and cardiac follow-up: confirm whether lipid panel, cardiology follow-up, and any ECG or stress testing are scheduled or overdue.

Substance use review: dependent drug abuse diagnosis (2018) with active opioid-type risk context; check for any new or refilled controlled substances, prescriber/pharmacy alerts, urine drug screen results, and counseling or treatment attendance; note interaction risk with current cardiac medications and sedation.
Chronic pain and migraine review: pain scores, migraine frequency and acute medication use days, any changes in analgesic or preventive therapy, and functional impact.
Weight and BMI trend (obesity history), plus dental status given impacted molars and any dental pain or extraction plans, and nutrition or dietary changes since cardiac diagnosis.

Function, cognition, mood, and caregiver: ADL/IADL changes, mobility aids, cognitive screen, depression/anxiety screen given cardiac diagnosis and pain burden, social supports, and attendance at PACE center; check care-plan items due in the window (assessments, reassessments, goal reviews) and confirm the team has a plan for discussing these changes.
